screening.reason: Analyses involuntary head-motion signatures derived from ABIDE I/II resting-state fMRI acquisitions in an explicit ASD-vs-TD group-difference (age-stratified) analysis; satisfies inclusion 2-3 (not a motion-correction method benchmark — the comparison itself is the autism-vs-control finding).

evidence_spans.text: This study includes all sites publicly available through ABIDE I and ABIDE II. They were comprised of 1,127 TD and 1,017 ASD.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was the full publicly available ABIDE I+II release: 1,127 TD and 1,017 ASD, stratified by age.

evidence_spans.text:
We find significant shifts in statistical features of typical
levels of involuntary head motions for different age groups.
evidence_spans.claim: Involuntary head-motion statistics (NSR, Gamma parameters) shift significantly across age groups in TD.

evidence_spans.text:
The results suggest that the levels of random involuntary
motor noise are elevated in autism across age groups.
evidence_spans.claim: Main finding: random involuntary motor noise (head micro-motion) is elevated in ASD relative to TD across age groups.

evidence_spans.text:
The comparisons of the age-groups with ASD also show shifting
statistical signatures across ages (Figure 5) and they were
significant at the 0.05 level for all comparisons in the NSR.
evidence_spans.claim: ASD age-group comparisons showed significant (p<0.05) shifts in the noise-to-signal ratio (NSR) of head motion across all age-group comparisons.

evidence_spans.text: The ABIDE data is publicly available. We have uploaded to ABIDE the indexes of the participants included in the current study.
evidence_spans.claim: Participant indices for this study were uploaded to ABIDE, enabling cohort reconstruction.

evidence_spans.text:
All methods and data types generated to produce the ﬁgures will be made available through Github, https://github.

evidence_spans.claim: Analysis code was made available on GitHub.

assessments.support: All ABIDE I/II sites used, N by diagnosis (1127 TD/1017 ASD) and age-group stratification stated; participant indices uploaded to ABIDE.
Multi-site (all ABIDE I/II sites), age-group breakdown by decade-scale bins given in Table 1.

Head motion (linear/angular speed) is derived from the standard rs-fMRI motion-correction/realignment step rather than connectivity; no named preprocessing pipeline/version is given for the underlying rs-fMRI data beyond the motion-parameter extraction itself.
ASD/TD labels taken from ABIDE phenotypic files; the diagnostic instrument is not restated in this paper.
Age is the primary stratification variable and the focus of the study; ABIDE's own age/sex matching is invoked, though site is pooled across all sites without a site covariate.
Bootstrapped resampling (n=25 per subgroup, 100 subgroups) used to standardize group sizes, but no explicit site-effect adjustment.

Outcome is a kinematic (Gamma-distributed noise-to-signal ratio of head motion) rather than a connectivity metric; validity for this specific construct is argued via prior work but is a departure from standard connectivity outcomes.

Kruskal-Wallis non-parametric ANOVA with pairwise group comparisons at p<0.05/0.01 is used; explicit multiple-comparison correction across all pairwise age-group tests is not detailed in the sections read.

risk_of_bias.summary: A well-specified, fully public, pan-ABIDE cohort with reconstructible participant indices, but the outcome is head-motion kinematics rather than functional connectivity, and multiple-comparison handling across many pairwise age-group tests is not fully detailed.

charting.title: Age-Dependent Statistical Changes of Involuntary Head Motion Signatures Across Autism and Controls of the ABIDE Repository
charting.age_range_controls: same age bins as ASD group
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — participant indices uploaded to ABIDE, and analysis code/figures available on GitHub
charting.specific_features: Linear and angular head-motion speed derived from rs-fMRI realignment; noise-to-signal ratio (NSR) and Gamma probability density function parameters of micro-movement spikes (MMS)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: Custom stochastic/Gamma-distribution analysis of head displacement/rotation parameters (no named connectivity pipeline)
charting.feature_change_direction: Elevated random involuntary motor noise (higher NSR) in ASD vs TD across age groups; both groups show age-dependent shifts but ASD shifts are non-uniform
charting.validation_methodology: Kruskal-Wallis non-parametric ANOVA for pairwise age-group comparisons
charting.summary_key_findings: Using all publicly available ABIDE I/II sites (1,017 ASD, 1,127 TD), stochastic (Gamma-distribution) signatures of involuntary head motion during resting-state fMRI shift significantly with age in TD, and ASD participants show significantly different, non-uniform age-dependent shifts, with overall elevated random involuntary motor noise relative to age-matched TD.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Elevated noise-to-signal ratio (involuntary motor noise) in head motion during resting-state scanning, differing non-uniformly by age in ASD vs TD
charting.future_directions_recommended: Use of age-appropriate statistical models for dynamically changing self-generated signals in ASD research
charting.reviewer_notes: Outcome is head-motion kinematics, not functional connectivity; included per protocol inclusion criteria since it is a resting-state-fMRI-derived autism-vs-control group-difference analysis, not a motion-correction method benchmark.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational), age-stratified; ABIDE I+II, all public sites; n=1,017 ASD / 1,127 TD.
narrative_row.methods: Linear/angular head-motion speed extracted from rs-fMRI realignment parameters; bootstrapped resampling (100 subgroups of n=25); Gamma-distribution stochastic-signature analysis (NSR, MMS); Kruskal-Wallis pairwise age-group comparisons.
narrative_row.outcomes: Involuntary head-motion statistics shift significantly with age in TD; ASD shows significantly different, non-uniform age-dependent shifts and overall elevated involuntary motor noise relative to age-matched TD.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Outcome is head-motion kinematics rather than functional connectivity; no named preprocessing pipeline for the underlying rs-fMRI; multiple-comparison correction across many pairwise tests not fully detailed; site pooled without explicit harmonisation.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Fully reconstructible cohort (participant indices uploaded to ABIDE, code on GitHub) spanning the whole public ABIDE I+II release, useful as a QC/motion covariate reference for other connectivity studies in the knowledge graph.
